claims.text: A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy engineered with coherent nanoprecipitates can exhibit a temperature-dependent ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
An HPHT-treated high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure can exhibit a temperature-dependent ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Complex composition and engineered microstructure prevent classical temper embrittlement in these high-entropy alloys.
The proposed starting material may be a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy or a eutectic high-entropy alloy in an as-cast or solution-treated state.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation produces coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent interfaces in the nanoprecipitate-strengthened tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent interfaces relieve stress concentrations that can otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
HPHT treatment can produce a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The HPHT-induced coherent-interface microstructure promotes multiple deformation mechanisms, including dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and deformation twins.
The engineered microstructure suppresses segregation of embrittling species.
Complex alloying in high-entropy alloys suppresses the impurity segregation responsible for temper embrittlement.
The proposed material is ductile at low temperature.
The proposed material becomes brittle within a narrow intermediate-temperature range because deformation mechanisms are insufficiently activated.
At higher temperature, the material regains ductility because dislocation mobility increases and multiple deformation mechanisms become active.
Conventional tungsten-based or nickel-based alloys display irreversible temper embrittlement within a narrow temperature window.
The reversible transition requires both a sufficiently complex high-entropy composition and coherent-interface microstructural engineering.
Conventional alloys or high-entropy alloys lacking the specified coherent-interface design will not show the same reversible ductile–brittle–ductile behavior.
